It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing the “noise and tumult” of a world where political powers grow cold toward the Gospel and seek to silence His messengers, and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the mandate of public witness and the limits of civil authority in this hour? [13, 252, 1331, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the sight of “savage wolves” who “do not spare the flock” or use the law as a “scourge” against the faithful, or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that “not one human sinner or demonic power will ever succeed in his rebellion” against the King? [13, 20, 253, 263, 368, 1143, 1425, 1471, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many seek “diplomatic relations” with a “distinctively anti-Christian agenda” to avoid the “scars” of the cross, we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Master personally governs the “record of history” by reminding us that our “citizenship is in heaven” [11, 15, 19, 28, 788, 1183, 1316, 1391, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the state’s attempt to criminalize your witness is not an “administrative anomaly” but is subject to the “decree from God” who “raises up kings, then pulls them from their thrones when they have served His administration” [15, 68, 252, 262, 585, 812, 1143, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Mandate to Obey the Higher King**

**Verse**
“But Peter and the other apostles answered and said: ‘We ought to obey God rather than men. The God of our fathers raised up Jesus whom you murdered by hanging on a tree. Him God has exalted to His right hand to be Prince and Savior, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins’ ” (Acts 5:29–31). [48, 914, 1078, 1130, 1176, 1205, 1247, 1249, 1256, 1300, 1431, 1529, 1720, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Scriptures reveal that the church has a “binding and authoritative mandate” from the Savior that no earthly “legislative body” can cancel or control [11, 15, 541, 785, 1316, 1503, 1720, Conversation History]. While we are commanded to “render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s,” the Reformed tradition—echoed by **John Calvin**—asserts that “Jesus Christ alone is the head of the church,” and we must “refuse to yield submission” to any ruler who tries to “tamper with or attempt to tone down the gospel” (Matthew 22:21; Colossians 1:18; Galatians 2:5) [19, 131, 293, 412, 1104, 1105, 1144, 1155, 1316, 1500, 1528, 1529, 1545, 1636, 1720, Conversation History]. Even when a state “makes havoc of the church,” the “Word of God is not chained” because “the Father has given Him authority over us” (2 Timothy 2:9; Colossians 1:18) [25, 41, 123, 293, 711, 1144, 1268, 1283, 1316, 1420, 1504, 1646, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” in “political maneuvering and lobbying” when the truth is at stake; instead, you must “be bold in our God to speak to you the gospel of God in much conflict” (1 Thessalonians 2:2) [51, 76, 91, 93, 123, 1017, 1406, 1461, 1503, 1670, Conversation History]. Recognize that “your life is not your own” because “you were bought at a price,” and your “sole objective” is to “adorn the doctrine of God” even if the “nations rage” (1 Corinthians 6:20; Titus 2:10; Psalm 2:1) [11, 12, 21, 101, 212, 265, 361, 529, 772, 879, 932, 1132, 1138, 1197, 1242, 1262, 1406, 1503, 1515, 1572, 1670, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, the “religious aristocracy” of the Sanhedrin often functioned as a “religious court,” but they were exposed as “usurpers” when they “rejected the word of the LORD” to maintain their own “political status” (1 Samuel 15:23; John 11:48) [15, 17, 174, 342, 1183, 1316, 1533, 1720, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our worship, revealing that “God is Spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth,” which means we do not need a “formal license” from a “governor” to be the true church (John 4:24) [13, 17, 23, 30, 31, 142, 860, 867, 923, 1313, 1426, 1445, 1529, 1611, 1636, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Limits of Ordained Submission**

**Verse**
“Let every soul be subject to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and the authorities that exist are appointed by God. Therefore whoever resists the authority resists the ordinance of God, and those who resist will bring judgment on themselves” (Romans 13:1–2). [925, 1105, 1202, 1233, 1246, 1284, 1342, 1422, 1473, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—upheld by **John MacArthur**—teaches that “secular courts” and governments are “ordained by God” for the purpose of maintaining “civil peace” and the “punishment of evildoers” [1036, 1233, 1341, 1473, Conversation History]. We are called to “lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and dignity,” showing that we are “loyal and submissive” to authorities in mundane matters (1 Timothy 2:2; 1 Peter 2:13) [77, 82, 93, 116, 925, 1105, 1284, 1473, 1709, Conversation History]. However, because “the judgment is God’s,” a ruler’s authority is limited; they act as a “terror” only to evil, not to the “spotless purity of truth” (Deuteronomy 1:17; Romans 13:3) [11, 37, 79, 131, 136, 575, 926, 1023, 1235, 1252, 1321, 1332, 1343, 1406, 1473, 1503, 1709, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by a “worldly philosophy” that suggests your primary battle is political; instead, you must “discipline your mind” to recognize that “the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh, but divinely powerful for the destruction of fortresses” (2 Corinthians 10:4) [43, 76, 91, 93, 1081, 1406, 1502, 1670, Conversation History]. “Trade in your worry for trust,” for the Lord will “respond to the prayer of the destitute,” and He will “keep you from the evil one” as you “honor the king” (Psalm 102:17; John 17:15; 1 Peter 2:17) [15, 39, 47, 68, 88, 94, 201, 872, 926, 1033, 1106, 1143, 1202, 1408, 1515, 1532, 1572, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Temporal Signs to Heavenly Hope**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “national greatness” and “dwelling in your land safely” were “temporal signs” of God’s blessing (Leviticus 26:5; Deuteronomy 8:19) [409, 620, 627, 755, 1342, 1353, 1519, 1546, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this, showing that the church is an “assembly of the citizens of heaven” who are “sojourners and pilgrims” on the earth (Philippians 3:20; 1 Peter 2:11) [13, 21, 26, 28, 38, 142, 440, 1023, 1203, 1313, 1320, 1326, 1426, 1529, Conversation History]. We look not for a physical “storage city” but for a “city whose builder and maker is God” (Hebrews 11:10) [26, 142, 242, 1233, 1251, 1257, 1313, 1426, 1529, 1646, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: God’s Sovereignty Over Persecution and Loss**

**Verse**
“ ‘But as for you, you meant evil against me; but God meant it for good, in order to bring it about as it is this day, to save many people alive’ ” (Genesis 50:20). [615, 663, 692, 735, 740, 1312, 1361, 1501, Conversation History]. “ ‘Remember the word that I said to you, “A servant is not greater than his master.” If they persecuted Me, they will also persecute you’ ” (John 15:20). [53, 617, 795, 893, 923, 942, 980, 1056, 1313, 1316, 1378, 1403, 1513, 1515, 1596, 1672, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Voddie Baucham**—asserts that God “harnesses the deeds of the wicked” to accomplish His “good and perfect ends,” even when those deeds involve the destruction of “holy and beautiful temple[s]” [5, 64, 600, 722, 1132, 1143, 1419, 1429, 1494, 1502, 1507, 1515, 1572, 1616, Conversation History]. When churches are physically destroyed or ministers are “commit[ed] to prison,” the Lord “remains with them” and uses the “horrible pit” of their suffering to “testify to the gospel of the grace of God” (Acts 20:24; Acts 8:3) [11, 31, 323, 656, 657, 711, 782, 840, 843, 861, 972, 973, 975, 1022, 1152, 1349, 1351, 1440, Conversation History]. This reveals that “nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan,” for He “declares the end from the beginning” (Isaiah 46:10) [11, 21, 64, 94, 121, 201, 1132, 1143, 1306, 1408, 1419, 1429, 1441, 1493, 1515, 1565, 1572, 1616, 1684, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “trade in your worry for trust,” knowing that “He who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ,” and no “administrative order” can erase your “inheritance incorruptible” (Philippians 1:6; 1 Peter 1:4) [5, 13, 21, 26, 83, 94, 102, 121, 142, 192, 201, 352, 442, 630, 829, 830, 1016, 1132, 1143, 1313, 1315, 1408, 1426, 1515, 1572, Conversation History]. You must “discipline your body and bring it into subjection,” refusing to let the “noise and tumult” of “savage wolves” frighten you, for “the Word of our God stands forever” while earthly “monument[s] of pride” will “vanish—like smoke they vanish away” (Isaiah 40:8; Psalm 102:3) [11, 20, 32, 79, 116, 121, 283, 702, 1306, 1313, 1374, 1406, 1515, 1684, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: The Invisible Temple**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “animal sacrifices” and physical sanctuaries were “shadows” that could not “eliminate sin” [11, 32, 394, 1313, 1344, 1430, 1442, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our vision of the sanctuary, revealing that “your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit,” making the believer a “portable temple” whose “victory” is found in “the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony” rather than in a physical building (1 Corinthians 6:19; Revelation 12:11) [11, 12, 13, 17, 21, 32, 92, 101, 186, 238, 240, 264, 402, 469, 790, 833, 937, 1054, 1059, 1093, 1202, 1208, 1219, 1220, 1243, 1262, 1267, 1313, 1315, 1402, 1403, 1406, 1417, 1426, 1491, 1503, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Final Reckoning for the Despot**

**Verse**
“Then the seventh angel sounded: And there were loud voices in heaven, saying, ‘The kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and of His Christ, and He shall reign forever and ever!’ ” (Revelation 11:15). [103, 133, 158, 174, 182, 650, 1199, 1315, 1524, 1636, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The biblical authors resolve the “noise and tumult” of “troublesome times” by fixating on the “consummation of history,” where “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” [13, 20, 21, 23, 24, 31, 103, 136, 182, 815, 1199, 1311, 1315, 1515, 1524, 1532, 1636, 1720, Conversation History]. Every ruler who “think[s] themselves much better than they really are” and seeks to “write themselves into God’s office” will ultimately be “weighed on the scales and found deficient” (Daniel 5:27) [11, 15, 30, 37, 324, 412, 1061, 1143, 1402, 1450, 1502, 1720, Conversation History]. On the Day of the Lord, He will “judge between the nations,” and His “everlasting dominion” will be the only kingdom that “shall not pass away” (Isaiah 2:4; Daniel 7:14) [11, 24, 37, 47, 92, 121, 176, 201, 210, 266, 278, 352, 412, 452, 470, 602, 614, 788, 825, 827, 855, 869, 903, 917, 940, 947, 958, 1035, 1113, 1132, 1143, 1183, 1233, 1259, 1260, 1266, 1268, 1288, 1290, 1300, 1301, 1306, 1311, 1312, 1315, 1402, 1408, 1420, 1450, 1460, 1473, 1515, 1519, 1684, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “perfect justice will come” and He will “wipe away every tear from their eyes” (1 Thessalonians 1:10; Revelation 21:4) [13, 14, 21, 24, 32, 92, 94, 109, 121, 201, 352, 470, 816, 822, 948, 1132, 1143, 1313, 1315, 1408, 1426, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. You can find “tranquility of soul” by resting on the “surest foundation,” for if God has “magnified Your word above all Your name,” His “unsearchable wisdom” is more than sufficient for your every need (Psalm 138:2; Ephesians 3:10) [11, 24, 47, 92, 121, 147, 176, 201, 352, 412, 602, 1132, 1143, 1408, 1420, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 87, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 300, 309, 324, 332, 361, 405, 413, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

God does not always deal as immediately and directly in physical ways with those who fail to uphold His holy character. But there will always be some consequence. Here are a few of the main ones: It gives the enemy an opportunity to blaspheme God. That is what Nathan told David (2 Sam. 12:14; cf. Ezek. 20:39; 1 Tim. 5:14; 6:1). God’s Word is dishonored (Titus 2:5). Sin can disqualify you from further service in the King’s court. Saul is the classic illustration of that (1 Sam. 15:23). You can lose your life or well-being (Acts 5:5, 10). God may withhold spiritual blessings (Num. 20:1–12). God’s anger is invoked (Isa. 5:25). God’s Spirit is grieved (Isa. 63:10).

We pray for each other to be worthy of our calling because Christ’s reputation is at stake. That was Daniel’s perspective when he prayed, “O Lord, hear! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, listen and take action! For Your own sake, O my God, do not delay, because Your city and Your people are called by Your name” (Dan. 9:19). One of the primary excuses people give for rejecting Christianity is hypocrisy manifest in the Christians they have met. Thus Paul prayed that we will be the opposite of hypocrites—that we will bring honor to the name of Christ and lead unbelievers to Him as a result. That’s why Jesus said, “Let your light shine before men in such a way that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven” (Matt. 5:16). Paul’s desire here is expressed no better than in his second epistle to the Corinthians: “As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker among you; as for our brethren, they are messengers of the churches, a glory to Christ” (2 Cor. 8:23).

Peter said when you humble yourself under God’s mighty hand, “He may exalt you at the proper time” (1 Peter 5:6). What’s the proper time? His time, not our time. When will it be? When He has accomplished His purpose. Now that might seem a little vague, but there’s no cause for concern: God has perfect timing. Indeed, our salvation depended on His perfect timing. Paul specified that the hope of eternal life was “at the proper time manifested” through Jesus Christ (Titus 1:2–3). Trusting in God’s timing is no light or peripheral matter to the Christian faith.

No one understood this principle better than the apostle Paul. As a “slave of Christ,” he had given up everything in order to serve His Master. His ministry was not an easy one, humanly speaking. He had been repeatedly beaten, imprisoned, endangered, and threatened with death. Yet in spite of it all, God always provided Paul with all that he needed to faithfully accomplish his ministry. “Be anxious for nothing,” he wrote to the Philippians, “but in everything by prayer and supplication . . . let your requests be made known to God” (4:6). Later in that chapter, he explained that he had learned the secret of being content, no matter his circumstances. Consequently, he could exclaim, “I can do all things through Him who strengthens me” (v. 13). Paul’s contentment came both from relying on Christ completely and also from rightly assessing his needs. As he explained to Timothy, “If we have food and covering, with these we shall be content” (1 Tim. 6:8).
